newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close higher, boosted by bonds.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close higher, boosted by bonds.

text.p: Argentine stocks snapped a soft streak Thursday and were seen ending the week on a firm note despite a 36-hour general strike.
Dealers said bolsa gains were driven by a rally in U.S. treasuries, which bolstered Argentine Brady debt.

"The markets reacted to a new decline in U.S. long bond yields," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "But bolsa buyers were selective and not so keen on heavyweight stocks listed abroad, like YPF."
The MerVal index rebounded 1.2 percent to 550.91, wiping out the week's slim losses.

"The MerVal faces pretty stiff resistance at 555 points and tomorrow it will probably stay hovering between 550-555," said Napoli. "We don't really expect a major fallout from the strike, but we will still be following events closely to gauge the level of support for the protest and the government's reaction."
The country's trade unions launched a 36-hour general strike against economic policy at midday (1100 EDT) Thursday, the second walkout in less than two months.
Traders said the market could be deserted Friday as many players take advantage of the strike for a long weekend break.
Floor volume remained weak at 12 million pesos Thursday but ironically picked up from a dismal tally of 9.8 million Wednesday, when the market anticipated the trading lull induced by the strike.
Over-the-counter volume, however, predictably shrank to 50.6 million pesos from 62.6 million Wednesday.
Winning issues bashed losers 36 to seven and 16 stocks closed flat.
Oil giant YPF, the bolsa bellwether, was one of only three main-tier losers, shedding 0.2 percent to 22.7 pesos. Traders said it had a firm international seller at 22.75.
The other decliners were oil company Sol Petroleo and agricultural holding company Capex, which dropped 1.0 percent and 0.6 percent, respectively.

Best MerVal performances were put in by strictly local issues. Textile and footwear firm Alpargatas jumped 4.2 percent, pulp and paper maker Celulosa gained 3.9 percent and carmaker Sevel closed up 2.9 percent.
